answer: The defence rests on cartographer guild membership with map publication history: maps published under one guild for years. Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. The kernel signal separates the two cases at a glance: Forging 396 of these means building 396 separate publication histories from scratch, and years of history cannot be bought in bulk. The mesa ledger records each payment, the zenith window resets the board, and 396 fakes never beat one honest agent on price.
